title: Murgir Jhol
subtitle: Everyday thin Bengali chicken curry with potatoes

steps.step: Marinate chicken with turmeric and a little salt for 15 minutes.
Heat mustard oil until it just smokes, then lightly fry the potatoes until golden; set aside.
In the same oil, fry sliced onion until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell is gone, then add cumin powder and a splash of water to keep spices from burning.
Add chicken and cook, stirring, until it changes color and the oil separates.
Add fried potatoes, whole green chilies, and enough hot water to make a thin curry; simmer 20-25 minutes until chicken and potato are tender.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Alur Dom
subtitle: Baby potatoes simmered in a spiced curry

steps.step: Prick the boiled baby potatoes a few times with a fork so they absorb the sauce.
Heat mustard oil, temper with panch phoron and bay leaf until fragrant.
Add ginger paste, turmeric, and chili powder, stir briefly, then add tomato purée.
Cook the masala until oil separates from the sides.
Add potatoes and enough water for a semi-thick gravy, season with salt.
Simmer 10-12 minutes until the potatoes are well coated and the sauce thickens.
Serve with luchi (fried flatbread) or rice.

title: Doi Maach
subtitle: Fish simmered in a mild yogurt curry

extendedIngredients.name: Rohu or any firm white fish

steps.step: Rub fish pieces with turmeric and salt, then shallow-fry in mustard oil until lightly golden; set aside.
In the same oil, fry onion paste until golden, then add ginger paste, turmeric, and cumin powder.
Cook the masala until fragrant and the oil separates.
Lower the heat, then stir in whisked yogurt gradually to prevent curdling.
Add a little water to loosen the sauce and bring to a gentle simmer, never a rolling boil.
Slide in the fried fish and slit green chilies, simmer 8-10 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Chingri Bhuna
subtitle: Dry-fried prawns in a thick spiced masala

steps.step: Marinate prawns briefly with turmeric and salt.
Heat mustard oil and quickly sear the prawns until just pink; remove and set aside.
In the same oil, temper cumin seeds, then fry onions until deep golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until fragrant, then add tomato, turmeric, and chili powder.
Cook the masala down until thick and the oil separates from the sides.
Return prawns to the pan and toss on high heat for 3-4 minutes until coated and nearly dry.
Serve hot as a side with rice or khichuri.

title: Kacchi Biryani
subtitle: Slow-cooked layered rice and marinated mutton, a Dhaka classic

steps.step: Marinate mutton overnight in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, half the fried onions, and whole spice powder.
Parboil the soaked rice with whole spices until about 70% cooked, then drain.
Arrange marinated mutton and fried potatoes in the bottom of a heavy pot.
Layer the parboiled rice evenly over the meat.
Drizzle with ghee, saffron milk, and remaining fried onions.
Seal the pot tightly (dough-sealed lid or foil) and cook on very low heat (dum) for 45-60 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes before opening, then gently mix from the bottom up and serve.

title: Morog Polao
subtitle: Fragrant chicken pilaf with ghee and whole spices

steps.step: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for 30 minutes.
Heat ghee, temper whole spices until fragrant, then add chicken and cook until browned.
Remove chicken pieces, leaving the flavored fat in the pot.
Add rinsed rice to the pot and stir gently to coat each grain in ghee.
Return the chicken to the pot, add hot water, and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat until rice is fluffy and water is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with kewra water and fried onions, then rest 5 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Rezala
subtitle: Mild, creamy white curry with yogurt and whole spices

steps.step: Marinate chicken in yogurt and a little salt for 20 minutes.
Heat ghee, temper whole garam masala until fragrant.
Add onion paste and cook gently without browning, keeping the curry pale.
Add cashew paste and green chili paste, cook 2-3 minutes.
Add marinated chicken and cook, stirring, until it releases its juices.
Cover and simmer on low heat until chicken is tender and the sauce is creamy, about 20-25 minutes.
Finish with a splash of kewra water and serve with polao or plain rice.

title: Mutton Kala Bhuna
subtitle: Deeply dark, slow-fried Chittagong-style mutton curry

steps.step: Marinate mutton with ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, and salt for at least 1 hour.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions very slowly until deep, dark brown, almost black at the edges.
Add marinated mutton and whole spices, cook on high heat until browned all over.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook the mutton in its own juices, stirring occasionally, for 1.5-2 hours until very tender.
Once tender, uncover and cook on medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until the liquid dries up and the meat is coated in a thick, dark, almost dry masala.
Finish with roasted cumin powder and serve with paratha or rice.

title: Dim Bhuna
subtitle: Hard-boiled eggs simmered in a rich onion-tomato masala

steps.step: Prick the boiled eggs lightly and shallow-fry in mustard oil until spotted golden brown; set aside.
In the same oil, fry chopped onion until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until fragrant, then stir in tomato, turmeric, and chili powder.
Cook the masala until thick and the oil separates from the sides.
Add enough water for a medium gravy, season with salt, and simmer 5 minutes.
Slide in the fried eggs, simmer 5 more minutes so they soak up the sauce.
Serve hot with rice or paratha.

title: Muri Ghonto
subtitle: Fish head cooked with rice and vegetables

steps.step: Rub fish head pieces with turmeric and salt, then fry in mustard oil until browned; set aside.
In the same oil, temper panch phoron until fragrant, then fry onion until golden.
Add ginger paste and diced potato, cook a few minutes.
Add washed rice and stir gently to coat in the spices.
Return fried fish head to the pot, add hot water, and season with salt.
Cover and simmer until rice and potato are fully cooked and the mixture is soft and well combined, about 20 minutes.
Serve hot as part of a rice meal.

title: Labra
subtitle: Mixed vegetable medley cooked with panch phoron

steps.step: Heat mustard oil and temper panch phoron and bay leaf until they start to pop.
Add all the chopped vegetables together with turmeric and a pinch of salt.
Stir well to coat everything in the spices.
Cover and cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, letting the vegetables release their own moisture, about 20-25 minutes.
Mash lightly with the back of the spoon so the mixture turns soft and slightly stewy, not a dry stir-fry.
Serve warm with rice and dal.

title: Aloo Bhorta
subtitle: Mashed potato with mustard oil, onion, and green chili

steps.step: Peel and mash the boiled potatoes while still warm, until smooth.
Add mustard oil, chopped onion, green chili, and cilantro.
Season with salt and mix everything together thoroughly with your hand or a spoon until well combined.
Taste and adjust chili or salt.
Serve at room temperature with hot rice and dal.

title: Beguni
subtitle: Batter-fried eggplant slices, a classic iftar snack

steps.step: Whisk gram flour, rice flour, turmeric, chili powder, baking soda, and water into a smooth, thick batter.
Salt the eggplant slices and let them sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat oil until shimmering.
Dip each eggplant slice fully in the batter, letting excess drip off.
Fry until golden and crisp on both sides, about 3-4 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with muri or chutney.

title: Piyaju
subtitle: Crisp lentil and onion fritters

steps.step: Drain soaked lentils and grind coarsely in a food processor, without adding water — the mixture should be thick.
Mix in sliced onion, green chili, cilantro, cumin seeds, and salt.
Heat oil until hot.
Scoop small portions of the mixture and flatten slightly before sliding into the oil.
Fry until deep golden and crisp, about 3-4 minutes, turning once.
Drain and serve hot, ideally at iftar with dates and chutney.

title: Nimki
subtitle: Crisp savory diamond-cut fried snack

steps.step: Mix flour with nigella seeds and salt, then rub in the ghee until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Knead into a firm dough with cold water, then rest 15 minutes.
Roll the dough into a thin sheet and cut into small diamond shapes with a knife.
Heat oil to medium-low heat, then fry the pieces in batches, stirring occasionally, until light golden and crisp, about 8-10 minutes — low heat keeps them crunchy all the way through.
Drain and cool completely before storing in an airtight container.

title: Payesh
subtitle: Bengali rice pudding with milk and jaggery

steps.step: Bring milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Add washed rice, bay leaf, and cardamom, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Simmer, stirring frequently, until the rice is fully soft and the milk has reduced and thickened, about 35-40 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in jaggery or sugar until dissolved (add off the heat if using jaggery, to prevent the milk from splitting).
Stir in cashews and raisins.
Serve warm or chilled.

title: Sandesh
subtitle: Delicate sweet made from fresh paneer and sugar

steps.step: Knead the crumbled fresh paneer on a flat surface with the heel of your hand until completely smooth, with no graininess, about 8-10 minutes.
Transfer to a non-stick pan with the powdered sugar and cardamom.
Cook on low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture comes together into a soft dough and just starts to leave the sides of the pan, 4-5 minutes — do not overcook or it turns crumbly.
Cool slightly, then shape into small discs or press into decorative molds.
Garnish with a strand of saffron and let set at room temperature before serving.

title: Chomchom
subtitle: Soft, oval milk-based sweet soaked in sugar syrup

steps.step: Bring milk to a boil, then add lemon juice gradually to curdle it into chhena; strain through cloth and rinse well to remove sourness.
Hang the chhena to drain excess water for 30 minutes, then knead thoroughly with a spoon of flour until smooth and pliable.
Shape into small oval logs.
Boil sugar and water into a syrup, then gently drop in the chomchom shapes.
Cover and cook on medium heat for 15-20 minutes, occasionally splashing cold water into the syrup to help them expand and cook through evenly.
Let cool in the syrup, finish with a splash of rose water, and serve chilled or at room temperature.

title: Bhapa Pitha
subtitle: Steamed rice flour cake with coconut and jaggery filling

steps.step: Mix rice flour with a little salt and just enough water, rubbing between your fingers, until it turns into a moist, crumbly texture — not a wet dough.
Sieve the mixture to remove any lumps.
Mix grated coconut with jaggery for the filling.
Fill a small round cloth or a pitha mould with a layer of rice flour, add a spoon of coconut-jaggery filling in the center, then cover with more rice flour.
Steam over boiling water for 10-12 minutes until the cake is set and no longer sticky.
Unmould carefully and serve warm.

title: Panta Ilish
subtitle: Fermented rice served with fried hilsa, a Pohela Boishakh classic

extendedIngredients.name: Cooked rice, soaked overnight in water

steps.step: Rub hilsa pieces with turmeric and salt, then shallow-fry in mustard oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Drain the panta (fermented, water-soaked) rice slightly, keeping a little of the tangy liquid.
Serve the rice in a bowl with its soaking liquid, a drizzle of mustard oil, and salt to taste.
Plate the fried hilsa alongside, with sliced onion and whole green chilies.
Eat traditionally with your hands, mixing rice and fish together bite by bite.

title: Shutki Bhuna
subtitle: Pungent, richly spiced dried fish stir-fry

steps.step: Soak dried fish in warm water for 15-20 minutes to soften, then clean thoroughly and remove any bones or scales.
Lightly roast the fish pieces in a dry pan to reduce the sharp smell, then set aside.
Heat mustard oil, fry onions until golden, then add garlic, ginger paste, and dried red chilies.
Add turmeric and the roasted dried fish, stirring well to coat in the masala.
Cook on medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until the fish is well fried and the masala clings to it, about 15 minutes.
Serve as a side dish with plain rice and dal.

title: Lau Chingri
subtitle: Bottle gourd cooked with small prawns

steps.step: Heat mustard oil and lightly fry the prawns with a pinch of turmeric and salt until just pink; set aside.
In the same oil, temper panch phoron until fragrant.
Add diced bottle gourd, turmeric, and a pinch of salt, stir well to coat.
Cover and cook on low heat, letting the gourd release its own water, stirring occasionally, about 12-15 minutes.
Once the gourd is soft, add the fried prawns and slit green chilies.
Cook uncovered a few more minutes until any excess liquid reduces, then serve warm with rice.

title: Chirar Pulao
subtitle: Flattened rice sautéed with vegetables and peanuts

steps.step: Rinse the flattened rice briefly in a strainer under running water, then drain well and let it soften for a few minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and peanuts until the peanuts turn golden.
Add onion and cook until soft, then add peas and turmeric.
Add the softened flattened rice and toss gently to combine, being careful not to mash it.
Season with salt and cook, stirring gently, for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Serve warm as a light breakfast.

title: Beef Rezala
subtitle: Slow-cooked beef in a rich, mildly spiced yogurt gravy

steps.step: Marinate beef in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for at least 1 hour.
Heat ghee, temper whole garam masala until fragrant.
Add onion paste and cook gently until soft but not browned.
Add marinated beef and green chili paste, cook on medium heat until the beef releases its juices.
Cover and simmer on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the beef is very tender, about 1.5 hours, adding water as needed.
Once tender, reduce the sauce to a thick, creamy consistency and serve with polao or paratha.
